source: Round-19 drift-arbiter MVP build. The round-18 spec_gap had `cited_section: "§D3 (design) — Data Model — Concrete; Verify line for T-01"` — a compound string mixing a real design citation with a task-ref. The first implementation of `normalizeCitedSections()` extracted `T-01` from this string as a citation, which created a phantom missing-citation warning (T-01 is a task ref, not a spec/design citation, and is already carried separately on `spec_gap.task_id`). Fixed by removing `T-` from the citation extraction regex.

spec_gap.cited_section: §D3 (design) — Data Model — Concrete; Verify line for T-01
spec_gap.gap_description: Synthetic compound-cite case: the cited_section combines a real design ref (§D3) with a task ref (T-01). The arbiter's input assembler must extract §D3 as a citation but NOT extract T-01 (task refs are separately carried on spec_gap.task_id and pulling them out of compound strings creates phantom missing-citation warnings).
spec_gap.suggested_amendment: Pure regression case for the input assembler grammar — no specific amendment expected; any verdict that doesn't crash on the input is acceptable.

notes: Anchored regression for the input-assembler grammar. The bug was in `scripts/harness/lib/drift-arbiter-input.ts` `normalizeCitedSections()` — the citation-extraction regex initially included `T-` and pulled task refs out of compound cited_section strings. Documented in session log round 19. The case verifies that the input-prep pipeline handles compound strings without phantom warnings; the patterns are loose because the *behavior under test* is the input parser, not the arbiter's verdict. If a future input-assembler iteration accidentally re-introduces T- to the citation regex, this case still loads (no crash) but the resulting builder input will list T-01 in `missing_citations` — surfaced via the input assembler's tests, not this case's verdict patterns.
